raw_task:
Review this B2B Group Sales MVP plan for a Finnish resort (Järvisydän, 40yo, ~50 staff). CEO needs it NEXT WEEK. Two salespeople (Sebastian + Jenni) starting outbound cold calling.

THE PLAN (8 micro-features, 10 weeks):
MF1 (Week 1): Customer registry — mine 1000 Word orders via Haiku Batch API → Excel. Sebastian can start calling.
MF2 (Week 2): Deal pipeline kanban (Excel + Obsidian Bases). 6 stages.
MF3 (Week 2-3): Hot Lead Surfacer — Python scorer, top 5 daily. Scoring: LTV(25), Recency(25), Active deals(20), Season(15), Call outcome(15).
MF4 (Week 3): Customer background package — auto-generated .md with booking history, preferences, allergies.
MF5 (Week 3-4): Call logger — Sebastian logs call outcomes (interested_now/later/not_now). Second brain for calls.
MF6 (Week 4-5): Email Drafter — 6 golden prompt types, Claude generates follow-up email 5min after call.
MF7 (Week 6-8): Scorer v2 — adds call trends, email engagement, win rates.
MF8 (Week 8-10): Power BI dashboard.

DATABASE: 6 Excel sheets (Companies 26cols, Contacts, Orders, Pipeline, Call Log, Email Log) → later Supabase.

COMPOUND FLYWHEEL: Every column designed to feed a later feature. Call outcomes → scoring. Email responses → prompt improvement. Won/lost → win rate per segment.

MINING: 1000 Word orders → python-docx → Haiku Batch API → JSON → Excel. Cost ~€2-3, ~2 hours.

CHALLENGE TWO THINGS:

1. Is 10 weeks too slow? Could we compress to 2-3 weeks using a long-running Claude Code agent that builds MF1-MF5 in one shot after the data mining is done? The mining (MF1) takes ~2h. After that, MF2-MF5 are just Python scripts + Excel formulas + Obsidian Bases configs. Could an agent ship these in 1-2 days instead of 4 weeks?

2. Is the plan MISSING anything critical for a B2B outbound sales operation? Sebastian starts cold calling next week — what will he need that isn't in this plan?

Be specific. Name what can be parallelized, what's truly sequential, and what's over-engineered for a 2-person team. 7/10 verbosity.
response:
Thought for 33s

Yes, the 10-week plan is too slow. CEO needs delivery next week and Sebastian + Jenni start outbound calls next week, so the MVP must be usable by Monday. The good news: the core (MF1–MF5) is almost entirely automatable and compressible to 3–4 working days total once mining finishes. No long-running “Claude Code agent” is required beyond what you can already do with Claude 3.5/Opus + Artifacts or Cursor — you can ship a working version in one shot.

1. Compression feasibility (MF1–MF5 in 1–2 days post-mining)

Mining (MF1) is the real 2-hour bottleneck and must run first (or overnight). It is truly sequential — you cannot score or generate background packages without the 1000-order JSON/Excel.

Everything after that is parallelizable and trivial for an agent:

Micro-feature	Effort	Can run in parallel with…	Agent can ship in…
MF2: Pipeline kanban (6-stage Excel + Obsidian Bases)	30 min (template + formulas)	Mining	Same afternoon
MF5: Call logger (simple sheet with dropdowns + timestamp)	20 min	Mining	Same afternoon
MF3: Hot Lead Surfacer (Python scorer + daily top-5 view)	45 min (one script + Excel refresh button)	Mining	Same afternoon
MF4: Background .md generator (python-docx + Claude prompt)	40 min (one script that reads row → calls Claude → saves .md)	Mining (once JSON ready)	Same afternoon

Realistic compressed timeline (you do this yourself or with Claude agent):

Day 1 (today/Tomorrow): Kick off Haiku Batch mining → output clean Excel (Companies + Orders + Contacts). While it runs, build MF2 + MF5 skeletons in Excel + share the file with Sebastian/Jenni.
Day 2 morning: Mining done → feed JSON to one Claude session. Ask it to output: (a) full Python scorer script, (b) background .md generator, (c) updated Excel with formulas/lookups. Test in <2 hours.
Day 2 afternoon: Hand Sebastian the Excel + scorer + one-click .md generator. He can call from the list immediately.
Day 3: Add MF6 Email Drafter (Claude prompt chain that reads Call Log row → generates email in Gmail draft). Total build time for MF1–MF6: ~1.5 developer-days.

What can be parallelized right now (even before mining finishes):

Create the 6 empty Excel sheets + basic column structure (Companies 26 cols, Pipeline, Call Log, etc.).
Write the 6 golden email prompt templates.
Draft a 1-page cold-call script + objection handler (Finnish + English versions) — Sebastian needs this tomorrow.
Set up Obsidian vault + Bases template (if you love it) or just stick to Excel for now.

What is truly sequential:

Any scoring or background generation (MF3/MF4) waits for mined data.
MF6 Email Drafter waits for Call Log entries.
MF7 (Scorer v2) and MF8 (Power BI) are post-MVP.

What is over-engineered for a 2-person team:

Scorer v2 (MF7) — call trends + email engagement + win rates can wait 4–6 weeks. v1 (LTV+Recency+etc.) is enough to start.
Power BI dashboard (MF8) — Excel pivot tables + one slicer dashboard is 90 % of the value for two salespeople. Power BI adds zero value until you have 200+ calls logged.
Obsidian Bases — nice-to-have “second brain”, but Sebastian/Jenni will live in the shared Excel. Drop it or make it optional.
6-stage pipeline is fine, but you only need 4 stages for week 1 (Contacted → Meeting Booked → Proposal → Won/Lost).

Result: Deliver MF1 + MF2 + MF3(v1) + MF4 + MF5 + basic MF6 by end of next week. Everything else is nice-to-have after they have closed their first 10 calls.

2. Critical gaps for B2B outbound (Sebastian starts calling next week)

The plan is strong on data flywheel but misses immediate execution necessities for cold/warm outbound group sales at a Finnish lakeside resort (corporate events, team days, conferences, incentive trips).

Must-add before next Monday (none of these exist in the 8 MFs):

Contact enrichment layer
Word orders give company name + maybe generic email. Sebastian cannot cold-call “ABC Oy”.
→ Add one column + simple Python/Haiku script that takes company name → outputs direct decision-maker name + phone + LinkedIn (use free Clay.com trial or Fonecta/Yritystieto.fi API). Do this in the same mining pass or as MF1.5 (30 min extra).
Cold-call script + Finnish objection handler
One shared Google Doc with:
30-second opener tailored to Järvisydän (sauna, lake activities, 40-year heritage).
5 most common objections + replies.
“Book a 15-min preview call” close.
Sebastian and Jenni need this tomorrow — they cannot improvise 100 calls.
GDPR / legitimate-interest tracker (Finland-specific)
B2B cold calling is allowed, but you must document “legitimate interest” per contact (past order = strong basis).
→ Add 2 columns in Call Log: “Legitimate Interest” (dropdown: Past customer / Public data / etc.) + “Do-Not-Call flag”. One click. Legal must-have, takes 5 min to add.
Calendar + proposal link
After a positive call they must instantly send a meeting link or “Järvisydän Group Offer” PDF.
→ Add Calendly/Outlook booking link column + one-click “Generate proposal” button (simple Word template + Python). Missing this kills momentum.
Daily KPI tracker (for you + CEO)
One tab: Calls attempted / Connected / Meetings booked / Pipeline value. Auto-calculates from Call Log + Pipeline. Sebastian/Jenni see their own leaderboard. Takes 15 min, delivers more insight than Power BI week 8.

Nice-to-have but not critical for week 1:

LinkedIn Sales Navigator research before calls (can be manual for first 50).
Email sequence automation (Instantly/Smartlead) — start with manual + MF6 drafter.
Trigger-event monitoring (new funding, job posts) — add in week 3.

Bottom line for Sebastian next week:
He needs one Excel file containing: enriched company list (sorted by scorer), call logger with GDPR column, pipeline kanban, one-click background .md, and the script link. That is the true MVP. Everything else (scorer v2, Power BI, Obsidian polish) is iteration, not launch.

Build the compressed version this week, hand it over Friday, and let the flywheel (calls → data → better scoring → better emails) start spinning Monday. The plan’s compound design is excellent — just ship the first 70 % in 4 days instead of 40. You’ve got this.
